prompt: You are now from Connecticut. Someone called it 'just a hallway between New York and Boston.' Defend your state with your whole chest.
response:
*A hallway?* 

First of all, pump the brakes, pull over into the right lane—because you’re probably camping in the left lane with out-of-state plates anyway—and wash your mouth out. 

If you think Connecticut is just the Merritt Parkway and an overpriced rest stop on I-95, you are driving with your eyes closed and you don't know what actual culture is. Let me educate you.

Let’s start with the most important thing: **Pizza.** Or as we call it, *apizza*. New York? Cute, floppy slices you have to fold to keep the grease from ruining your shoes. Boston? Don't even get me started on whatever doughy, thick-crust nonsense they’re serving up there. Look at New Haven. Sally’s. Pepe’s. Modern. We have the undisputed, globally recognized best pizza in the United States. We invented the white clam pie. It’s called *char*, not a burnt crust. Learn the difference before you disrespect us.

While we're on food, we also invented the *hamburger* (shoutout Louis' Lunch), and more importantly, we invented the **correct** way to eat a lobster roll. Hot. Dripping in melted butter on a toasted split-top bun. None of that cold mayonnaise Maine/Boston tragedy. We actually respect the seafood.

You want champions? **UConn Basketball.** We are the basketball capital of the world, men and women. Full stop. No one else is doing what Storrs is doing. 

You want history and brains? Yale. Mark Twain looked at the whole country and chose to live in Hartford. We gave the world the first nuclear submarine, the helicopter, the dictionary, and the freaking color television. 

You look at us as a "hallway"? Take an exit, buddy. Drive up into the Litchfield Hills in October. People pay thousands of dollars just to rent an Airbnb and pretend they live in *Gilmore Girls* for exactly one weekend. Go down to Mystic. Go to the Farmington Valley. We have colonial towns older than America itself, rolling mountains, and actual coastlines. We get the perfect four seasons without the apocalyptic blizzards of Massachusetts or the rat-infested garbage mountains of NYC. 

We aren’t the hallway between New York and Boston. We’re the master suite. New York and Boston are just our loud, obnoxious, overpriced neighbors. 

So next time you're stuck in traffic on the Q Bridge, don't complain. Sit there, breathe in the salt air from the Long Island Sound, be grateful you are within a ten-mile radius of a decent slice of apizza, and show some damn respect to the Nutmeg State.
